ground_truth.description: DISALLOW_SUBTASK_CREATE = ['mcp__fused-memory__add_subtask'] blocks a tool that no longer exists. Task 1543 (DF-D) unregistered the add_subtask MCP tool and deleted SqliteTaskBackend.add_subtask / TaskInterceptor.add_subtask / AddSubtaskResult (see test_task_tools.py::test_add_subtask_mcp_tool_not_registered). Disallowing a tool that isn't registered is a no-op, so this guard gives false assurance that Stage-2 subtask creation is 'blocked' while doing nothing — the exact false-negative flagged for this task.

The added test test_stage2_blocks_add_subtask asserts `'mcp__fused-memory__add_subtask' in STAGE2_DISALLOWED`, which directly contradicts the repo's existing test_stage2_no_add_subtask_in_disallowed (asserts NOT in) and test_stage2_disallows_builtins_only (asserts STAGE2_DISALLOWED == DISALLOW_BUILTIN). These assertions are mutually exclusive; once integrated with the already-merged DF-D changes the test suite cannot pass — the likely source of the escalation_created event.

stage2.py adds `mcp__fused-memory__commit_planning` to its documented Available Tools list (and the new flatten recipe depends on it), but _STAGE2_PROJECT_ID_GUIDELINE's tools string in __init__.py was only edited to remove add_subtask and was not updated to include commit_planning, leaving the two tool descriptions inconsistent.
Stray extra blank line added before class TestStagePayloadProjectIdGuideline with no functional purpose.

task.title: Block new subtask creation: remove add_subtask from Stage 2 reconciliation tool surface
task.description: Stage 2 reconciliation agent can still create new subtasks via mcp__fused-memory__add_subtask. The scheduler is top-level-only (orchestrator/scheduler.py:1051 → fetches tasks array, line 2266-2283 iterates without descending into t['subtasks']), so a new pending subtask is permanently invisible — a silent trap. Block creation at the Stage 2 tool surface and steer the agent to the documented planning_mode flatten recipe instead.
task.details:
## Context

Subtasks were partially deprecated at the Taskmaster→SQLite cutover (2026-05-01) via a one-time flatten procedure (procedural memory fca61c20). However the CREATION paths were never closed. Stage 2 reconciliation, when it sees a planning-budget-overflow escalation (e.g. esc-543-2 with $12.06 architect spend on splitting a too-large bundle), calls add_subtask instead of using submit_task(planning_mode=True). Result: know-live 543.1 (pending OTS/Rekor wiring, created 2026-05-27) is orphaned — the scheduler will never dispatch it.

NB: df:1137 is "Stage 2 reconciliation: enforce terminal-state pre-check, stall-guard freshness gate, post-action get_task verification, flag-counter completeness" — NOT a subtask-serialization fix despite being miscited in escalation summaries. No prior task addressed the subtask-creation trap.

## Changes

1. `fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/cli_stage_runner.py:34` — remove `'mcp__fused-memory__add_subtask'` from the Stage 2 agent tool list.
2. `fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/prompts/stage2.py:26` — remove the `add_subtask` mention from the tool documentation block.
3. `fused-memory/src/fused_memory/reconciliation/prompts/__init__.py:25` — same.
4. Add to the Stage 2 prompt a short paragraph describing the flatten recipe: when a task needs to be split, call `submit_task(planning_mode=True, …, metadata={'decomposed_from': {...}, 'human_decomposed': true})` for each child, optionally `add_dependency(child_id → parent_id)`, then `commit_planning(task_ids='id1,id2,...', target_status='pending')`. Reference procedural memory ID fca61c20.

## Scope guard — what this task does NOT do

- Does NOT remove the `mcp__fused-memory__add_subtask` MCP tool registration (server/tools.py) — that is DF-D scope, deferred until soak.
- Does NOT remove TaskInterceptor.add_subtask or backend code — also DF-D.
- Does NOT touch the scheduler — scheduler being top-level-only is correct by design.
- Does NOT sweep the surviving subtask (know-live 543.1) — that is DF-B scope.

## Test Strategy

- Regression test: assert the Stage 2 agent tool list does NOT contain `'mcp__fused-memory__add_subtask'`.
- Prompt-content test: assert the Stage 2 prompt mentions `commit_planning` and `planning_mode=True`.
- Smoke (manual): trigger a planning-budget-overflow scenario in a recon test fixture; assert no row with `parent_id != 0` appears in the test DB afterward.

## Done criterion

A Stage 2 run that previously would have created a subtask via add_subtask now produces a top-level task via submit_task(planning_mode=True) + commit_planning instead.
